So, I was able to create a website out of voat's source code. I'm posting this because there's no proper guide on how to set this up. Hope it'll help someone in the future. Shout out to @PuttItOut & @FuzzyWords for helping me to solve my problems.

Requirements :

  1. MS Windows
  2. Visual Studio Community
  3. SQL Express
  4. SQL Server Management Studio
  5. IIS

Step 1 - Setting up databases

First go ahead and install SQL Express and SQL Server Management Studio. Then open up SSMS authenticate with SQL Express (windows authentication). Right click on databases and create 2 databases named 'voat' & 'voatusers'. Then right click on Logins under security and create a new login. In the next window;

  1. Type in a login name
  2. Select SQL server authentication
  3. Type in a password
  4. Mark everything in Server roles tab
  5. In user mapping, select voat & voatusers and mark everything from the bottom section
  6. Click OK

Step 2 - Compile and Publish voat

Download the code from github. You have to use Dev(recommended) or Beta branch. Master is outdated. Once downloaded, extract it and;

  1. In Voat.Data | Create a copy of ~App.Config and name it App.Config
  2. In Voat.Tests | Create a copy of ~App.Config and name it App.Config
  3. In Voat.UI | Create a copy of ~web.Config and name it App.Config
  4. In voat.UI | Create a sitemap.xml file if you don't find it

Then open up Voat.sln. Then Go to Tools > Nuget Package Manager > Manage nuget packages for solution. You should see a pop up asking to restore missing packages. Click on restore. In the installed tab, search for SendGrid and uninstall the latest version from Voat.UI and install v6.3.4. Then build Voat.UI from Build section. You'll see a bunch of warnings and 0 errors. Warnings are expected. Now let's publish the project from Build > Publish Voat.UI

Step 3 - Hosting

Go to Voat/SqlScripts/ in your downloaded voat project and execute 2 sql scripts in SSMS

Open up the published folder and open the web.config in a notepad. * Set up <connectionStrings> according to your SQL server settings. * Under <voat.CacheHandler> section "Change the enabled setting to true on nullcache one and false in the others"

Now open IIS. Right click on sites > add a website. Give a site name and set the physical path to our published voat folder. Type in a hostname and you should have your own voat clone .
